title: Feasibility and acceptance of the use of intensive care diaries, created with the help of artificial intelligence, in the context of everyday intensive care – an exploratory mixed-method pilot study
summary:
This study investigates whether it is possible and useful to use automatically generated intensive care diaries for patients. These diaries are created using artificial intelligence (AI) from the medical and nursing records of the intensive care unit.

Who participates?
Patients who are conscious again in the intensive care unit and can give their consent.
They must have been in the intensive care unit for at least three days.
They will soon be transferred to a normal ward or rehabilitation.

Procedure:
Four weeks after their stay in intensive care, patients receive their AI-generated diary.
The diary is reviewed together with a nurse specialist.
No later than four weeks after that, an interview is conducted to ask about the patients' experiences.

Objective:
The aim is to determine how many patients are eligible for the study and how well the process works.
conditions: Post-Intensive Care Syndrome (PICS) and associated psychosocial stress in adult intensive care patients

interventions.name: Receiving an AI-generated intensive care diary based on personal intensive care and intensive medical documentation

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Stay on the intensive care unit for more than 72 hours 
Cognitive and emotional stability to read and understand the intensive care diary  
Patient regained consciousness in intensive care 
Patient is capable of giving consent 
Patient does not have an intensive care diary 
Signed consent form from the patient available 
Electronic patient documentation available 
At the time of the interview, the patient is located within a maximum radius of 60 km from Lübeck, Schleswig-Holstein
Exclusion criteria:
Pre-existing and documented mental illness
Stay on the intensive care for more than 28 days
Withdrawal from the study due to death, withdrawal of consent or failure to attend the interview appointment
